proof_spine: A derivative candidate is an epsilon-delta relation.
Two derivative candidates at the same point are equal.
Differentiability gives existence, and uniqueness selects derivative_at(f, x).
The selected derivative of ode_solution is 2 * x, so it satisfies the ODE through the value interface.

blocks.intent: Define epsilon-delta control for a candidate slope.
blocks.accepted_litex:
prop derivative_delta_controlled(f fn(x R) R, x0, slope R, epsilon, delta R+):
    forall x R:
        x != x0
        abs(x - x0) < delta
        =>:
            abs((f(x) - f(x0)) / (x - x0) - slope) < epsilon

blocks.intent: Replay the checked epsilon-delta proof for the tracer solution.
blocks.accepted_litex:
thm ode_solution_has_derivative:
    ? forall x0 R:
        $has_derivative_at(ode_solution, x0, 2 * x0)
    claim:
        ? forall epsilon R+:
            exist delta R+ st {$derivative_delta_controlled(ode_solution, x0, 2 * x0, epsilon, delta)}
        witness exist delta R+ st {$derivative_delta_controlled(ode_solution, x0, 2 * x0, epsilon, delta)} from epsilon:
            claim:
                ? forall x R:
                    x != x0
                    abs(x - x0) < epsilon
                    =>:
                        abs((ode_solution(x) - ode_solution(x0)) / (x - x0) - 2 * x0) < epsilon
                x - x0 != 0
                ode_solution(x) = x^2 + 1
                ode_solution(x0) = x0^2 + 1
                ode_solution(x) - ode_solution(x0) = (x^2 + 1) - (x0^2 + 1) = x^2 - x0^2 = (x - x0) * (x + x0)
                (ode_solution(x) - ode_solution(x0)) / (x - x0) = x + x0
                (ode_solution(x) - ode_solution(x0)) / (x - x0) - 2 * x0 = x - x0
                abs((ode_solution(x) - ode_solution(x0)) / (x - x0) - 2 * x0) = abs(x - x0) < epsilon
            by def $derivative_delta_controlled(ode_solution, x0, 2 * x0, epsilon, delta)
    by def $has_derivative_at(ode_solution, x0, 2 * x0)
blocks.reusable_lesson: The existing proof establishes the concrete candidate slope needed by the selected-value tracer.

blocks.intent: Replay the original witness-oriented ODE theorem.
blocks.accepted_litex:
thm ode_solution_solves_equation:
    ? forall x R:
        $solves_ode_at(ode_solution, ode_rhs, x)
    witness $solves_ode_at(ode_solution, ode_rhs, x) from 2 * x:
        by thm ode_solution_has_derivative(x) => $has_derivative_at(ode_solution, x, 2 * x)
        ode_rhs(x, ode_solution(x)) = 2 * x
blocks.reusable_lesson: The old relational consumer remains valid alongside the new value consumer.
The initial value stays independent of the derivative interface extension.

blocks.intent: Select the unique derivative value on differentiable inputs.

attempts.verifier_evidence: session block B014A1 ok:true; trace normalizes the declaration to have fn derivative_at as set

blocks.accepted_litex:
have fn derivative_at by exist!:
    ? forall f fn(t R) R, x0 R:
        $is_differentiable_at(f, x0)
        =>:
            exist! slope R st {$has_derivative_at(f, x0, slope)}
    obtain chosen_slope from $is_differentiable_at(f, x0)
    claim:
        ? forall slope1, slope2 R:
            $has_derivative_at(f, x0, slope1)
            $has_derivative_at(f, x0, slope2)
            =>:
                slope1 = slope2
        by thm derivative_value_unique(f, x0, slope1, slope2)
    exist! slope R st {$has_derivative_at(f, x0, slope)}
blocks.reusable_lesson: Conditional unique existence creates a derivative function whose valid use is guarded by is_differentiable_at.

blocks.intent: Bridge a proved derivative candidate to the selected derivative value.
blocks.accepted_litex:
thm has_derivative_at_to_derivative_value:
    ? forall f fn(t R) R, x0, slope R:
        $has_derivative_at(f, x0, slope)
        =>:
            $is_differentiable_at(f, x0)
            derivative_at(f, x0) = slope
    witness $is_differentiable_at(f, x0) from slope:
        $has_derivative_at(f, x0, slope)
    slope = derivative_at(f, x0)
    derivative_at(f, x0) = slope
blocks.reusable_lesson: Prove with has_derivative_at, then consume the result as an equality for derivative_at.

blocks.intent: Define the value-oriented ODE solution relation.
blocks.accepted_litex:
prop solves_ode_at_by_derivative(f fn(t R) R, rhs fn(t, y R) R, x R):
    $is_differentiable_at(f, x)
    derivative_at(f, x) = rhs(x, f(x))
blocks.reusable_lesson: A value-oriented ODE predicate must retain differentiability as the guard for derivative_at.

blocks.intent: Expose the tracer solution's derivative as a selected value.
blocks.accepted_litex:
thm ode_solution_derivative_value:
    ? forall x R:
        $is_differentiable_at(ode_solution, x)
        derivative_at(ode_solution, x) = 2 * x
    by thm ode_solution_has_derivative(x) => $has_derivative_at(ode_solution, x, 2 * x)
    by thm has_derivative_at_to_derivative_value(ode_solution, x, 2 * x)
blocks.reusable_lesson: The relational proof is converted once into the reader-facing derivative equality.

blocks.intent: Prove the ODE through the selected derivative value interface.
blocks.accepted_litex:
thm ode_solution_solves_equation_by_derivative:
    ? forall x R:
        $solves_ode_at_by_derivative(ode_solution, ode_rhs, x)
    by thm ode_solution_derivative_value(x)
    ode_rhs(x, ode_solution(x)) = 2 * x
    derivative_at(ode_solution, x) = ode_rhs(x, ode_solution(x))
    by def $solves_ode_at_by_derivative(ode_solution, ode_rhs, x)
blocks.reusable_lesson: ODE consumers can read derivative_at(f, x) = rhs(x, f(x)) once differentiability is carried in the predicate.
